```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

gambitR3D is multilevel chess in R: three fixed 4×4 boards and four movable
2×2 platforms, 64 physical squares that keep their identity when platforms
move. The package plays, records, analyses and teaches the game, and can train
a small transformer opponent. Everything runs locally; nothing needs a network
connection, an account or Python unless you choose to train a model.

The rules are an experimental project convention (`experimental-v0.1`), not an
official rulebook. `vignette("rules", package = "gambitR3D")` explains them.

## The app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Opens the local app in your browser, bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
gambitR3D::g3_run_app()
```

Play hotseat or against the computer, switch between the 2D boards and the 3D
scene, show the Neutral board highest or lowest, then save, analyse and review
the game. `vignette("app", package = "gambitR3D")` is the tour.

## A game in R

A game holds its initial state, the current state and an event log. The rules
functions work on the state.

```{r}
game <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game(players = list(white = "Ada", black = "Computer"))
acts <- gambitR3D::g3_legal_actions(game$state)
nrow(acts)
head(acts[, c("action_id", "label")])
```

Every action has a stable id. Squares are named `board:u:v`; the label adds
the board and the projected coordinate, so `W:b3` and `N:b3` are never
confused even though they share a coordinate.

```{r}
game <- gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(game, "m:W:1:1-N:1:1")
reply <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(game$state, agent = "search",
                                     budget = list(nodes = 20000L))
reply$label
reply$status
game <- gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(game, reply$action_id)
gambitR3D::g3_game_moves(game)[, c("ply", "actor", "notation")]
```

The search reports how deep it completed, how many positions it visited and
its score in heuristic units from the side to act's point of view. These are
not centipawns: piece values for this variant are unknown.

A whole game against the computer:

```{r}
play <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()
while (!gambitR3D::g3_is_terminal(play$state) && play$state$ply < 30L) {
  agent <- if (play$state$side == "white") "search" else "greedy"
  d <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(play$state, agent = agent, budget = list(nodes = 5000L))
  play <- gambitR3D::g3_game_apply(play, d$action_id)
}
if (!gambitR3D::g3_is_terminal(play$state)) {
  # A ply cap is a truncation, never a draw.
  play <- gambitR3D::g3_game_event(play, "truncated", reason = "vignette ply cap")
}
play$metadata[c("result", "termination")]
```

## Saving and loading

Games are saved in the native JSON format. Every action is replayed through
the rules on loading, and any checksum mismatch is rejected.

```{r}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".g3.json")
gambitR3D::g3_write_game(play, path)
back <- gambitR3D::g3_read_game(path)
identical(gambitR3D::g3_game_hash(back), gambitR3D::g3_game_hash(play))
```

FEN and PGN cannot describe platforms or overlapping squares, so they are
neither read nor written.
